texts.preamble: M/S.Dharmapal Satyapal Ltd vs State Of Kerala on 3 October, 2012 Author: V.K.Mohanan Bench: V.K.Mohanan In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr.Justice V.K.Mohanan Monday,The 8Th Day Of July 2013/17Th Ashadha, 1935 WP(C).No. 14199 of 2013 (Y) ---------------------------------------- Petitioner: ------------------- M/S.Dharmapal Satyapal Ltd., 6/163 B, C.D.E, K.B.A Complex, Kjodappilly, Pathalam, Ernakulam, 683 501, Represented By Its Senior Manager - Mr.V.R.Shivakumar. By Advs.Sri.Anil D. Nair, Sri.J.R.Prem Navaz, Smt.Nivedita A.Kamath, Sri.Sreejith.R. Nair. Respondents: ------------------------ 1. State Of Kerala, Represented By Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Kerala , Ernakulam- 682 031 . M/S.Dharmapal Satyapal Ltd vs State Of Kerala on 3 October, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8771342/ 1 2. Commissioner Of Food Safety, Government Of Kerala,Trivandrum- 695 001. By Sr. Government Pleader Sri. Tom.K.Jose. This Writ Petition (Civil) Having Come Up For Admission On 03-07-2013, The Court On 08-07-2013 Delivered The Following: Prv. W.P.(C).No.14199/2013-Y: Appendix Petitioner'S Exhibits: Exhibit P1: True Copy Of The Writ Appeal Bearing No 1685/2012 Filed By The Petitioner. Exhibit P2: True Copy Of The Order In W.A No 1685 Of 2012 Dated 03-10-2012. Exhibit P3: True Copy Of The F I R Dated 28-04-2013. Exhibit P4: True Copy Of The Seizure Mahazar Dated 28-04-2013. Exhibit P5: True Copies Of The Licenses Granted To The Petitioner By The Competent Authorities At Chennai To Sell And Distribute The Subject Products Panmasala In The State Of Kerala. Exhibit P6: True Copies Of The Enlarged Labeling And The Contents On Each Pouch Of Panmasala . Exhibit P7: True Copies Of The Invoice, Sugam E-Form Way Bill. Respondents' Exhibits: Nil. M/S.Dharmapal Satyapal Ltd vs State Of Kerala on 3 October, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8771342/ 2 //True Copy// P.A. To Judge. Prv. V.K.Mohanan, J. ------------------------------- W.P.(C) No.14199 of 2013 ------------------------------- Dated this the 8th day of July, 2013. J U D G M E N T
texts.facts: The petitioner is a public limited company and claims that they are engaged in manufacturing and trading of various food items amongst others including, salts, spices, soda water, dry fruits, mouth freshener, mineral water, 'panmasala' without containing tobacco or nicotine as an ingredient, which are manufactured and sold under various brands including "Rajnigandha". The petitioner claims that it has got requisite permission, sanctions, and licenses for manufacture and production as well as sale of the aforesaid items of food in the country. According to the petitioner, the cause of action for filing the present writ petition arose as the 1st respondent State has seized certain boxes containing 'panmasala' under the brand name 'Rajnigandha', which according to the petitioner is a non tobacco based product, under serious misconception and error that the seized items contain tobacco which is a prohibited article in the State of Kerala and further aggrieved by the crime, which was registered as Crime No.524/13 in the Walayar police station. According to the petitioner, the above goods were seized when the same being transported by M/s. Royal Enterprises, which is one of the distributors of the petitioner company in the State of Kerala, from Bangalore depot to the State of Kerala, under the erroneous presumption that the panmasala, which was being transported, contains tobacco or nicotine and therefore the same are liable to be seized. 2. It is the further case of the petitioner company that the products manufactured by the petitioner and sold through its distributors, dealers, retailers among others are governed by the Food Safety and Standard Act 2006 and Food Safety and Standards (Food Product Standards and Food Additives) Regulations 2011 made therein and the petitioner has all permissions, sanctions and licenses from the competent authority to manufacture the said goods, over this country including the State of Kerala. According to the petitioner, the Government of Kerala, which is the 1st respondent in the above writ petition, has passed an order prohibiting the manufacture, the stockage, the sale or the distribution of 'Gutka' and 'panmasala' containing tobacco or nicotine as ingredients, in whatever the name in which it is available in market in the State of Kerala, with the observation that 'panmasala' is an article of food in which Tobacco and nicotine are used as ingredients and therefore the State Government, being satisfied with the expediency to prohibit M/S.Dharmapal Satyapal Ltd vs State Of Kerala on 3 October, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8771342/ 3 gutka and panmasala as the food products, in which tobacco and nicotine are widely used as ingredients, prohibited the same vide circular No.A-1327/12/CFS dated 25.5.2012. According to the petitioner, aggrieved by the above circular, initially they approached this Court by filing W.P.(C) No.12352/12 and connected cases. When the above writ petition came up for consideration along with identical matters, a learned Judge of this Court issued a common order dated 2.8.2012, by which it is concluded that, "It appears that during the pendency of the writ petitions and during the hearing of the matter, various items have been confiscated and kept sealed. After the impugned notification was issued, a circular dated 29.5.2012 produced as Ext.R2(1) in W.P.(C) No.12352/2012 was issued, by which time was granted upto 15.6.2012 for removing the articles from the State. The apprehension of the petitioners is that the confiscated articles will be readily destroyed. In the light of the order refusing stay of the notification impugned, it is only proper that time is granted for removal of the articles, for which a fresh order/circular will be issued." Aggrieved by the above order, the petitioner herein who is the petitioner in W.P.(C) No.12352 of 2012 and the connected ones, preferred an appeal before this Court ie., W.A.No.1685/12 and according to the petitioner, a Division Bench of this Court by order dated 3.10.2012 in the above writ appeal, had clarified that the intention behind the Government order is to prohibit or ban production, distribution and sale of gutka and panmasala containing tobacco or nicotine as ingredients, by whatsoever name they are available in the market in the State of Kerala. Ext.P2 is the above order of the Division Bench of this Court. So according to the petitioner, the petitioner's company being the manufacturers of various food items and Rajnigandha flavoured panmasala is one among its products, it is a standardised food product as per the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 and the same does not come under the purview of the Notification/ Government Order issued by the State Government of Kerala as the said notification is for imposing ban only on panmasala containing tobacco/nicotine and according to the petitioner, the said fact is clarified by the Division Bench of this Court as per Ext.P2 order. 6. As directed by this Court, the 2nd respondent herein had filed a statement on 28.6.2013 and another statement by the Sub Inspector of police, Walayar police station.
texts.arguments: 3. It is the further contention of the petitioner that the food items now seized do not contain tobacco and the products containing tobacco is called 'gutka' and the same cannot be termed as Panmasala. It is the further case of the petitioner that, as I indicated earlier, the goods now seized do not contain tobacco or nicotine and it is not a 'gutka' product. But the respondents have seized the same without any proper authority and seized in gross violation of the guidelines and directions contained in the above referred Government order and ignoring the clarification issued by Division Bench of this Court as per Ext.P2 order. Therefore, the petitioner approached this Court by filing the above writ petition under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India, praying inter alia the following : "(a) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of a writ of Mandamus directing the respondents not to detain, confiscate, and seize any goods which are not covered by circular bearing reference No: A-1327/12/CFS dated 25.5.2012 and as clarified by the judgment of the Division Bench of this Hon'ble Court in W.A.No.1685 of 2012 dated 3.10.2012. (b) direct the release of the consignment seized by respondent No.1 and subject matter of Crime No.524 of 2013 registered with Walayar Police Station, Palakkad, M/S.Dharmapal Satyapal Ltd vs State Of Kerala on 3 October, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8771342/ 4 State of Kerala. (c ) to grant stay of all further proceedings pursuant to Exhibit P3 pending final disposal of the writ petition (d) issue such other and further reliefs as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the interest of justice." 4. Heard Adv.Sri.Deepak Dhingare learned senior counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Tom K.Thomas Special Government Pleader to A.G. 5. The learned senior counsel for the petitioner through his persuasive arguments, it is submitted, after having invited my attention to Ext.P1 order of the learned single Judge of this Court and Ext.P2 order of Division Bench of this Court, particularly the circular No.A- 1327/12/CFS dated 29.5.2012 issued from the office of the Commissioner of Food Safety, Government of Kerala, that 'Rajnigandha' - a branded panmasala product of the petitioner's company, contains no tobacco or nicotine as an ingredient, to attract legal or penal proceedings against the petitioner or its product 'Rajanigandha'. According to the learned counsel, the respondent State has no authority to detain or confiscate or seize any goods which are not covered by the above circular and as clarified by Ext.P2 order of the Division Bench of this Court. According to the learned counsel, the product of panmasala is defined under the Food Safety and Standards (Food Product Standards and Food Additives) Regulations 2011, which describes 'Panmasala' under Regulation '2.11.5' and thus according to the learned counsel, the ingredient of Rajnigandha is only panmasala and the same contains no tobacco or nicotine and according to the learned counsel, if the 'panmasala' contains tobacco, then it is called 'Gutka' and therefore the same cannot be 'panmasala'. It is the further submission of the learned counsel that, the consignment of 'Rajnigandha' - the panmasala, a product of the petitioner company and which is the subject matter of invoice No.11/C013/000003 dated 24.4.2013 of the petitioner, was transported to M/s Royal Enterprises, Alappuzha, through ABT parcel service vide L.R.No.29076 dated 24.4.2013, was seized by the Commercial Tax Officer, Walayar check post, without any authority and sanction of law. According to the learned counsel, the Commercial Tax Officer, Walayar check post, has seized the product of the petitioner company erroneously and under serious misconception that the seized items are tobacco products. After showing me the container of 'Rajnigandha', it is the submission of the learned counsel that the ingredients shown on the cover are only permissible ingredients and therefore there is no violation of any statutory mandate or procedure and no penal liability is attracted. Learned counsel strenuously submitted that if the officers or the agents of the State are permitted to make such illegal seizure, it will affect the right of the petitioner and the same will amounts to interference with the commerce and trade being conducted by the petitioner company. Therefore, according to the learned counsel, the petitioner company is entitled to get released the seized article, which is the subject matter of Crime No.524/13 of Walayar police station. Sticking upon the above statement, the learned Government Pleader submitted that as per the provisions of the Food Safety M/S.Dharmapal Satyapal Ltd vs State Of Kerala on 3 October, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8771342/ 5 and Standard Act 2006, the authorities constituted under the above Act are empowered to search, seize, investigate and prosecute any offence relating to food. The learned Government Pleader submitted that the food which was seized and which is the subject matter of the crime, comes within the definition of 'Food' as contemplated under the above Act. According to the learned Government Pleader, the question whether the food products transported by the petitioner were adulterated or contain nicotine or tobacco or whether the petitioner has violated any provisions of the Food Safety and Standard Act, or the Regulation thereunder can be decided only on the basis of chemical analysis report upon the samples drawn from the seized article. However, in paragraph 3 of the statement dated 1.7.2013 it is stated that "In the above circumstances, this Honourable Court may be pleased to direct the Magistrate Court to release the seized articles to the District Food Safety Officer, Palakkad, for further action as contemplated under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006."
